title: The app mints Periodicals by id; no grant decision reads prompt text
description:
## Goal

The app's Periodical **Mint** and **Mint + Autopilot** actions send `{ periodicalId, autopilot }` and let the server render the prompt, as the proxy mint route does (LIN-4313). Then no lane decides the dispatch grant by reading prompt text.

## Context

Today the UI posts the already-rendered prompt (`buildPeriodicalNodes` → `autopilotPrompt`). The session lane then decides whether to declare the dispatch grant by checking whether that text contains `PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, M2b, around line 1227). That is an authority decision made by sniffing client-sent text. The proxy mint route renders on the server and decides from a flag. Both Surveys of LIN-4317 (at `c491eca5`) name this as the real cure. LIN-4317 only gives the two lanes one shared rule with two inputs.

## This step

* **The UI's two Periodical actions post the id and the variant;** the server renders with `renderPeriodicalPrompt`.
* **The session lane declares the grant from the variant flag,** not from text.
* **Any remaining reader of the tail-in-text check** either goes, or keeps a recorded reason.
* **The existing grant witnesses** (owner declared, non-owner refused, plain leaf) and the byte-pinned prompts stay green.

**Not this ticket:** changing any Periodical's prompt text.

## Done when

* No grant decision reads prompt text.
* The UI's Mint and Mint + Autopilot dispatch the same pinned prompt bytes as before.
* The grant tests and E2E pass.

(Runs after LIN-4317, which touches the same rule.)

## From LIN-4317's blind reads (6 Nov, at `f2816e17`): pulled here

Four blind, code-only reads scored LIN-4317 and LIN-4313 + LIN-4317 **better, better**. Under the stop rule there's no tidy-after; their residues in this area come here, as claims to check:

* **A missed copy of the name.** `lib/periodical-runs.js:117` still writes `` `${t.title} + Autopilot` `` by hand, so `periodicalPromptName` (`lib/periodicals.js`) has a copy it missed.
* **The forward comment.** Comments now say "LIN-4318 is the cure" and "LIN-4317 holds the reason". When this ticket removes the text sniffing, rewrite them to say what the code does now, with no ticket pointers.
* **Re-checked preconditions.** On the mint lane, `declaresPeriodicalGrant` re-checks preconditions that are already true (a literal `kind: 'periodical'`, an id already validated). Once the session lane passes a flag too, say where the preconditions live, once.

comments.body:
## Drift & Coherence run 5 (LIN-4324): the grant input is client-posted text

Found by the second read of the run-5 window (`af55cb73..5c63aa26`). This is the input question this ticket already names, with a trust consequence it does not state.

On the session lane the dispatch grant is declared from prompt text the browser posts: `declaresDispatchGrant` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1226-1227`) passes `isAutopilotVariant(prompt)`, which is `prompt.includes(PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL)` (`lib/periodicals.js:1131`). `public/app.js:1620-1626` posts the rendered prompt. The mint lane takes the route's `autopilot` flag instead (`dispatch-entrance.js:2008`). The owner check at the mint remains the authority, so the consequence is a grant decided on client-composed text, not an escalation. `lib/periodical-runs.js:117` also hard-codes the `+ Autopilot` name.

Acceptance, for the owner to decide: the session lane declares the grant from the server's own record of the variant, not from the posted text; `lib/periodical-runs.js:117` uses `periodicalPromptName`.

Run-5 report, row 141 (LIN-4324). No ticket was minted; this is the home.
